name: camera2d
description: The view onto the world: a camera is an entity with a Position that the screen is centred on, a zoom, and optionally a target it follows. Without a camera, the world is drawn as is, one world unit per pixel.

components.name: Camera
components.description: Marks the entity whose Position is at the centre of the screen. zoom 2 shows everything twice as big. If several entities have a Camera, the oldest one is used.

components.name: CameraTarget
components.description: Marks the entity that the Camera follows. If several entities have it, the oldest one is followed.

components.name: CameraFollow
components.description: Makes the Camera's entity move towards the CameraTarget each tick. stiffness is the share of the distance covered per tick: 1 sticks to the target, 0.1 trails it smoothly, 0 does not follow. follow_x and follow_y turn an axis off (a camera that only scrolls up and down keeps follow_x false). offset_y puts the camera that many units below the target (y grows downwards), so a target that climbs is shown above the middle of the screen. only_up makes the camera never move down (y never grows): a climber that falls back does not drag the view with it. offset_x is the same for x (the camera is that many units to the right of the target), and only_down, only_left and only_right are the three other directions of only_up: a runner whose camera never goes back uses only_right. dead_x and dead_y make a dead zone: while the target stays within that distance of where the camera aims, the camera does not move, and past it the camera only follows the part that goes beyond (small steps and jumps leave the view still). look_ahead aims that far ahead of the target along x, on the side its Velocity goes, so that a moving character sees more of what comes. bounded keeps the view inside the area from (bound_left, bound_top) to (bound_right, bound_bottom): the edges of the level are never passed, whatever the size of the window, and an area smaller than the view is centred.

components.name: CameraShake
components.description: Shakes the view of the Camera's entity: while strength is more than 0, the picture is moved by up to strength world units in every direction, speed times a second, and strength goes down by decay units a second until it is 0 again. A game shakes the camera by setting strength (a fall, a blow, an explosion); the camera's Position is left alone, only the drawing moves.

components.name: CameraFit
components.description: Makes the Camera's entity show a whole area of the world, whatever the shape of the screen: each tick (before drawing) its zoom and Position are set so that the area width by height, centred on (center_x, center_y), is as big as it can be in the window while still fitting entirely. The margins (pixels of the window) keep room at the edges for an interface (a score at the top, buttons at the bottom): the area is centred in what is left. max_zoom, when it is more than 0, stops the area from being enlarged past that zoom (a small board is not blown up on a huge screen). A board, a level seen at once, a map.

systems.name: follow
systems.description: Moves every Camera that has a CameraFollow towards the CameraTarget's Position (and ahead of its Velocity), then keeps its view within its bounds.

systems.name: apply
systems.description: Tells the renderer where the camera is (shaken by its CameraShake) and how far it is zoomed, before the frame's drawing systems run. Presentation only: it never changes the simulation.

systems.name: settle
systems.description: Lowers the strength of every CameraShake by its decay, down to 0.

systems.name: fit
systems.description: Sets the zoom and the Position of every Camera that has a CameraFit so that its area fits the window (the Viewport) inside its margins.
